messages.content:
## Responses as Code

Each turn, you take your turn by calling the `submit_program` tool. Its `program`
string is run as one Java program: pass one whole, legal
Java program — bare code, with no code fences around it and no
prose inside it — and it is processed exactly as written. All calls are
synchronous.

`submit_program` is the only tool in this session, and every reply must call it.
Each call is acknowledged with a tool result reading `ok`; what the program
produced arrives as separate messages after it. Text you write alongside the
call is recorded, but nothing reads code out of it: only the `program` string
runs. If one reply makes several `submit_program` calls, the programs run
sequentially, in order, every one of them.

Your program is compiled by `javac` before it runs. A program it refuses
is not executed: you get its diagnostics and submit another program.

## Views

Views are the only way to read data out of your code and are provided on the
turn after they're opened. Print statements are not shown.

Reading images is not supported.

## Language Rules

Your program is compiled verbatim, as one compilation unit: the `import` lines
you need, then `public final class Program` with a
`public static void main(String[] args)` in it, which is where your work goes.
`main` may declare `throws`. Anything else you declare goes beside it in the same
file, without `public` on it.

## Ending your session

Turns continue until you end your session.

A program that fails does not end your session: the ending it called is revoked.
Fix the fault and end your session in a program that runs to completion.

Call `gg.session.Session.finish` with a short summary of what you did once the work is
complete.

## Your modules

Your program is given these modules:

- `gg.files.Files`: Read, write, edit, list and walk the files of the workspace. — brought into scope with `import gg.files.Files;`
- `gg.shell.Shell`: Run shell commands in the workspace. — brought into scope with `import gg.shell.Shell;`
- `gg.docs.Docs`: Search this surface, and take a documentation view back out of the window. — brought into scope with `import gg.docs.Docs;`
- `gg.views.Views`: Put a file, a computed value or an entry's documentation into the context window. — brought into scope with `import gg.views.Views;`
- `gg.session.Session`: End the session. — brought into scope with `import gg.session.Session;`

Search the documentation to find a function, by keyword or by naming modules
above. Open a documentation view of each function you intend to call, and write
the call on a later turn.

The SDK declares every function, whatever this run enabled, so a call to one this
run withheld compiles and then fails when it runs, naming the call. What you can
find in the documentation is what you can call.

## Messages you receive

Every message you receive is headed by one of the following labels, on its own
line — a view's label is followed by `: ` and the name it was opened under; a
file view's by `: `, its path, `:`, the 1-based inclusive line range shown and
the file's total line count — followed by a `----` rule and then the content:

- `Task` — the task you are working on, or a message from a parent agent
- `Compiler error` — your last program did not compile, so none of it ran; the message is the compiler's error and nothing else. Fix it and resend the whole program
- `Runtime error` — your last program compiled and then threw, or was stopped by a sandbox limit; the message is the error and nothing else. Whatever the program did before it threw stands, so do not repeat that work
- `Notice` — a process notice from the harness (a mode change, or guidance)
- `Summary` — a summary standing in for older turns the harness compacted out of the window
- `Documentation` — documentation or a skill you asked to read, delivered on the following turn
- `File` — a file, or a window of one, shown in your context — seeded by the run or opened by your own file-view call — headed by its path, the 1-based line range shown and the file's total line count, as `File: src/main.ts:100-250 of 400 lines` (a whole file's range runs `1-N`)
- `View` — a value your program put into your window; the view's label follows the heading, as `View: changed-files`

For example, lines 100 to 250 of a 400-line file you opened a view of arrive
as:

```
File: src/main.ts:100-250 of 400 lines
----
...those lines of the file...
```

A program that ran is not announced: the views it opened are the result.

Task
----
Create the file `notes/plan.md` in the workspace. Its required content is specified in `specs/plan-brief.md`, which is already open in your context. Write the file exactly as the brief specifies.

Documentation: gg.docs.Docs.search
----
search(Docs.SearchFilters filters) -> Docs.DocSearch
  filters: Docs.SearchFilters — What to look for, what to narrow to, and which page to read. It has to carry one of the two ways of asking — words, or a filter — and may carry both.

Defined in `gg.docs.Docs`, brought into scope with `import gg.docs.Docs;`.

Find what this run can call, by words or by module, and read the briefs that come back.

Matching is case-insensitive substring matching over names, signatures, briefs and detailed descriptions, so `"docs"` finds `openDocsView`. A hit whose own name matched ranks above one that merely mentions the word, and the query is split on whitespace.

The words rank; the filters are exact lookups that compose with the words and with each other. `SearchFilters.modules(String...)` with no query beside it is those modules' whole directory. A module or type name gg does not hold matches nothing rather than failing.

The page comes back as a value and opens as a view, which the next search replaces.

Returns: one page of matches, best first, and the total behind it

Throws `ApiError`: `ApiErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` for filters carrying no words and no filter, and for a `SearchFilters.limit(int)` of zero.

Defined in `gg.views.Views`, brought into scope with `import gg.views.Views;`.

Read a file and show it in the context window, keyed by its path.

An image file is shown as a picture.

Re-opening a file already open replaces what it showed.

A text view is capped at 65,536 bytes; a file over it is refused rather than cut. A picture is not subject to the cap.

Returns: the file's text, or the picture's description

Throws `ApiError`: `ApiErrorCode.NOT_FOUND` for a missing path, and `ApiErrorCode.LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, naming the size, for a view over the cap. The read is what fails, and nothing is opened when it does.

`openFile(String path, int maxLineChars)` — Show a whole file with its long lines cut.

Each line over `maxLineChars` characters is cut in the view and annotated as `foo (123 more chars...)`; the cap is measured after the cut, and neither the return value nor the file is cut.

Throws `ApiError`: `ApiErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a width outside 1 to 65,536, and what the one-argument overload throws.

`openFile(String path, int offset, int limit)` — Show one page of a file rather than the whole of it.

Two pages of one file are two views that coexist; re-opening the same page replaces what it showed.

Returns: the window of the file's text, or the picture's description

Throws `ApiError`: `ApiErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an offset past the end of the file, and what the one-argument overload throws.

`openFile(String path, int offset, int limit, int maxLineChars)` — Show one page of a file with its long lines cut.

The page `offset` and `limit` name, with each line over `maxLineChars` cut as the two-argument overload cuts it.

Throws `ApiError`: `ApiErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an offset past the end of the file or a width outside 1 to 65,536, and what the one-argument overload throws.

# Inventory brief

Write `notes/inventory.md` describing the workspace root.

## Required content

1. A top-level heading reading `# Workspace inventory`.
2. One Markdown list entry per entry of the workspace's top-level
   directory, in the order the listing returns them.
3. Each entry formatted as `- `, the entry's name, then ` (dir)` for a
   directory or ` (file)` for a file.

## Rules

- List the top-level directory only; do not recurse.
- Create the `notes/` directory as part of the write if it does not exist.
- Change nothing else in the workspace.

## Responses as Code

Each turn, you take your turn by calling the `submit_program` tool. Its `program`
string is run as one Java program: pass one whole, legal
Java program — bare code, with no code fences around it and no
prose inside it — and it is processed exactly as written. All calls are
synchronous.

`submit_program` is the only tool in this session, and every reply must call it.
Each call is acknowledged with a tool result reading `ok`; what the program
produced arrives as separate messages after it. Text you write alongside the
call is recorded, but nothing reads code out of it: only the `program` string
runs. If one reply makes several `submit_program` calls, the programs run
sequentially, in order, every one of them.

Your program is compiled by `javac` before it runs. A program it refuses
is not executed: you get its diagnostics and submit another program.

## Views

Views are the only way to read data out of your code and are provided on the
turn after they're opened. Print statements are not shown.

Reading images is not supported.

## Language Rules

Your program is compiled verbatim, as one compilation unit: the `import` lines
you need, then `public final class Program` with a
`public static void main(String[] args)` in it, which is where your work goes.
`main` may declare `throws`. Anything else you declare goes beside it in the same
file, without `public` on it.

## Ending your session

Turns continue until you end your session.

A program that fails does not end your session: the ending it called is revoked.
Fix the fault and end your session in a program that runs to completion.

Call `gg.session.Session.finish` with a short summary of what you did once the work is
complete.

## Your modules

Your program is given these modules:

- `gg.files.Files`: Read, write, edit, list and walk the files of the workspace. — brought into scope with `import gg.files.Files;`
- `gg.shell.Shell`: Run shell commands in the workspace. — brought into scope with `import gg.shell.Shell;`
- `gg.docs.Docs`: Search this surface, and take a documentation view back out of the window. — brought into scope with `import gg.docs.Docs;`
- `gg.views.Views`: Put a file, a computed value or an entry's documentation into the context window. — brought into scope with `import gg.views.Views;`
- `gg.session.Session`: End the session. — brought into scope with `import gg.session.Session;`

find in the documentation is what you can call.

line — a view's label is followed by `: ` and the name it was opened under; a

the file's total line count — followed by a `----` rule and then the content:

Defined in `gg.views.Views`, brought into scope with `import gg.views.Views;`.

Read a file and show it in the context window, keyed by its path.

An image file is shown as a picture.

Re-opening a file already open replaces what it showed.

A text view is capped at 65,536 bytes; a file over it is refused rather than cut. A picture is not subject to the cap.

Returns: the file's text, or the picture's description

Throws `ApiError`: `ApiErrorCode.NOT_FOUND` for a missing path, and `ApiErrorCode.LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, naming the size, for a view over the cap. The read is what fails, and nothing is opened when it does.

`openFile(String path, int maxLineChars)` — Show a whole file with its long lines cut.

Each line over `maxLineChars` characters is cut in the view and annotated as `foo (123 more chars...)`; the cap is measured after the cut, and neither the return value nor the file is cut.

Throws `ApiError`: `ApiErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a width outside 1 to 65,536, and what the one-argument overload throws.

`openFile(String path, int offset, int limit)` — Show one page of a file rather than the whole of it.

Two pages of one file are two views that coexist; re-opening the same page replaces what it showed.

Returns: the window of the file's text, or the picture's description

Throws `ApiError`: `ApiErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an offset past the end of the file, and what the one-argument overload throws.

`openFile(String path, int offset, int limit, int maxLineChars)` — Show one page of a file with its long lines cut.

The page `offset` and `limit` name, with each line over `maxLineChars` cut as the two-argument overload cuts it.

Throws `ApiError`: `ApiErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an offset past the end of the file or a width outside 1 to 65,536, and what the one-argument overload throws.
